top_story.headline: Virginia House challenger's campaign reports fraud on its bank account, and says an FEC analyst told it to report the charges as expenses
top_story.dek: Joy for Virginia filed a Form 99 on October 15 describing fraudulent activity on its campaign account.
paragraphs: Joy for Virginia, the committee of Democratic House challenger Joy Powers (Virginia), told the Federal Election Commission in a Form 99 received October 15 that it found fraudulent activity on its campaign bank account. The committee says it spoke with an FEC staffer named Michael at about 18:30 that day. At his instruction, it says, it filed the fraudulent expenses under Line 21 of its Form 3 while it pursues the matter with the financial institution. It promised more information to the FEC when available. The filing gives no dollar amount, no dates of the transactions and no account details, and it does not say who is suspected. The keyword hit is a lead and not a finding: the filing describes a loss to the committee, not misconduct by it.

Two other filings from the batch concern large corrections. Huerta Democracy PAC told FEC analyst Aaron Carrell on October 16 that outside counsel is reviewing how it calculated independent expenditures on its July Quarterly Report (05/14/2026–06/30/2026). The PAC says its preliminary review indicates some amounts may have been reported on an overinclusive basis, including general overhead and personnel costs. It says the review covers hundreds of accounting transactions and asks for the additional time it discussed with the Reports Analysis Division. Rolling Sea Action Fund says it filed amendments on October 15 reaching back to the first quarter of 2024 after a self-audit of cash on hand and Line 8 discrepancies that an FEC request for additional information (RFAI) dated February 24, 2026 had raised.

sections.headline: Two House Democrats explain reporting errors in Form 99 letters
paragraphs: Two sitting members filed Form 99 correspondence this window. Both are routine fixes to dates and debt reporting. Neither involves a termination.

items: Rep. Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY), committee Clarke for Congress, Form 99 received 10/15, the response due date. This answers an FEC request about inconsistent debt reporting on the April 2026 Quarterly Report. The debt to Berger Hirschberg Strategies carried an incorrect date because of an administrative oversight; the committee says the date is fixed in an amended April Quarterly. The debt to Katz Compliance was not correctly linked to a repayment because of an administrative oversight and a software error. An amended Year-End 2025 Report adds a $2,800 debt incurred 12/15/25 and shows an 11/04/25 payment resolving a $2,844.52 debt incurred 8/6/25. Signed by treasurer Una Clarke. Filing.

Rep. Diana DeGette (D-CO), committee Diana DeGette for Congress, Form 99 received 10/16. While preparing the 48-hour report for 6/14/26, the committee found a discrepancy in the receipt dates of two contributions, from Kurken Alyanakian and Deborah Shpall. Both were made through ActBlue on 6/12/26 and appeared in the July Quarterly as received 6/12, but the committee received them 6/14/26. The Form 99 explains the difference and corrects the receipt date. Filing.

sections.headline: 55 Form 99s: about a dozen answer FEC inquiries, most are below-$5,000 threshold statements
paragraphs: This batch is the usual post-quarterly-deadline pile. No RFAI letters themselves were in the input. Roughly a dozen Form 99s are replies to FEC inquiries, including corrections of cash on hand, receipt dates and allocation. Many others are small campaigns telling the FEC they never crossed the $5,000 registration or reporting threshold.

One keyword hit, Asian Americans for Civil Rights and Equality Action Fund, comes from the confidentiality footer of a law firm email, not from any allegation. Every filing is listed below with its own link.

items: Asian Americans for Civil Rights and Equality Action Fund (PAC/party filer, type I), received 10/14. The filing is a copy of a 10/14 email from Destiny R. Snyder, a post-bar law clerk at Keys Law Corporation in Sacramento, requesting an e-filing password for committee C90023631. It is followed by an FEC envelope replacement page. The "unauthorized use" keyword hit is the email's standard confidentiality disclaimer. Filing.

Joy for Virginia (House candidate committee; Joy Powers, D-VA challenger), received 10/15. Reports fraudulent activity on the campaign bank account and says it filed the fraudulent expenses under Line 21 of its Form 3 on an FEC staffer's instruction while pursuing the matter with the bank. See the Top Story. Filing.

Abteen Vaziri for Congress (House candidate committee; Abteen Vaziri, R-TX challenger), received 10/15. The committee amended its July 2026 Quarterly Report (FEC-2027773) to correct beginning cash on hand. It blames a software carry-forward error in reports filed through another vendor. Amendments to the Year-End 2025, 12-Day Pre-Primary and April 2026 Quarterly Reports are being filed this week to reconcile cash on hand with bank records. Filing.
Alaine Elizabeth Giuliani (presidential candidate committee, no party), received 10/16. Says there are "no monies to report" for the October Quarterly. Filing.

Albritton for Congress (House candidate committee; Devinche Javon Albritton, independent challenger, VA), received 10/16. Says the committee has not crossed the $5,000 threshold in contributions or expenditures. Filing.

Antonio Srado for Congress (House candidate committee; Antonio Srado, R-FL challenger), received 10/14. Requests termination of its voluntary registration. It says it never exceeded $5,000, the campaign has ended, and it has $0 cash and no debts or loans. An FEC termination approval for the committee appears in the Terminations Wire. Filing.

Barton for Congress (House candidate committee; Keith George Barton, R-TX open seat), received 10/16. Says the candidate received less than $500 in campaign donations in the third quarter of 2026. Filing.

Brandon Conceicao for Congress (House candidate committee; Brandon Conceicao, NH challenger), received 10/16. Says it did not raise or spend more than $5,000 as of October 14, 2026, the end of the 12-Day Pre-General coverage period, so it was not required to file that report. Filing.
Brent for Congress (House candidate committee, FL address), received 10/14. Says the committee has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Filing.

Building America's Republican Representation PAC (PAC, type Q), received 10/16. Responds to an FEC letter on its July Monthly Report (06/01/2026–06/30/2026), received 7/22/2026. It says it did receive the contribution from Independent Agents & Brokers of America, Inc. PAC that it reported, and attaches a copy of the item. The reply does not state what the FEC questioned. Signed by treasurer Paul Kilgore. Filing.

Burgess Foster for Congress (House candidate committee; Burgess Foster, D-MI open seat), received 10/16. The candidate believed he would hit the threshold but, after a second review, was short of $5,000, and submits the statement as a waiver. Filing.

Chauna Banks for Congress (House candidate committee; Chauna Banks, D-LA challenger), received 10/16. Says she has not raised or spent more than $5,000 by the end of the October Quarterly period and therefore need not file it. The filing is itself the public-record statement she says she intends to file. Filing.

Chris for Congress (House candidate committee; Christopher Johnson II, independent challenger, MA), received 10/16. Says the committee has not met the $5,000 threshold for registration or disclosure. Filing.
Christopher for Congress (House candidate committee; Christopher Ajluni, independent, AZ open seat), received 10/16. Says the campaign has not raised more than $5,000. Filing.

Christopher Schmidt for Congress (House candidate committee; Christopher Schmidt, independent, NY-21 open seat), received 10/14. Says the campaign did not exceed $5,000 in contributions or expenditures in the third quarter of 2026 and is not required to file a standard quarterly report. Filing.

Committee to Elect Marlon Duran (House candidate committee; Marlon Gerardo Duran, Green Party, TX challenger), received 10/15. Says the campaign did not meet the $5,000 fundraising threshold for July–September 2026. Filing.
Cope for Georgia (House candidate committee; Benjamin M. Cope, R-GA open seat), received 10/16. Says the committee has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold. Filing.

Cranmer for Congress (House candidate committee; Andrew Ira Cranmer, Libertarian, KS challenger), received 10/16. Says it has not raised or spent more than $5,000 in the 2026 cycle as of the October Report's coverage end date and is not required to file it. Filing.

Defending the American Dream PAC (PAC, type Q), received 10/16. Replies to an RFAI dated 10/15/2026. After speaking with FEC staffer Sarah Vivian, it says item one was actually a discrepancy in Line 8 of Column B. It amended its September Monthly Report (listed as 8/01/2026–8/31/2026), saying the year-to-date totals were off from a data entry error and the period figures were correct. Signed by treasurer Ashley Ragan. Filing.

Democratic Party of Virginia (state party committee, type Y), received 10/14. Replies to an RFAI dated September 29, 2026 on its August Monthly Report. It amended its Statement of Organization to disclose the depository in question. After reviewing with the analyst, it says the H3 transfers and totals for administrative and direct fundraising activity were reported and aggregated correctly, so no amendment appears necessary. Signed by assistant treasurer John Roberson. Filing.
Dena Maldonado (House candidate committee; Dena Marie Maldonado, R-CA open seat), received 10/16. Says she had no financials over $5,000 for the special election. Filing.

Derito for Congress (House candidate committee; Adam Derito, R-CO challenger), received 10/15, labeled a disavowal response. The text reads only "Password test response to FEC File. Please ignore." Filing.

Edward Codelia for Congress (House candidate committee, HI address), received 10/16. Certifies that it received no contributions, loans or transfers and made no expenditures during the period. Filing.
Elect Doctor Astronaut (presidential candidate committee; candidate listed as Doctor Astronaut, R), received 10/15. Says the committee has not raised or spent $5,000. Filing.

Eric Shaw for Congress (House candidate committee; Eric Shaw, D-CA open seat), received 10/14. Says total receipts and disbursements have not exceeded $5,000 in the 2026 cycle and that there was no reportable activity from July 1 to September 30, 2026. It says it remains in a "testing the waters" capacity, has no debts, and is not seeking termination. Filing.

Fred Francis 2028, Inc. (presidential candidate committee; Fred Hagin Francis, D), received 10/14. Late disclosure by the committee's own account: it apologizes that Form 1 was not filed on time. It says it wrongly believed the form was required only after a contribution threshold, and filed it immediately on learning otherwise. Filing.

Frese for Congress (House candidate committee; Jeffrey Frese, R-CA-10 challenger), received 10/16. Says it has not exceeded $5,000 through October 14, 2026, the close of books for the Pre-General Report, and is not required to file it. It will begin filing Form 3 reports if it passes the threshold. Filing.

Friends of Michael Heidenreich (House candidate committee; Michael Heidenreich, D-WI challenger), received 10/16. Says he did not raise and disburse more than $5,000 in total during the campaign and is deciding whether to convert the committee to a PAC. Filing.

Friends of Roy Cho Inc. (House candidate committee; Roy Cho, D-NJ challenger), received 10/16, labeled a debt settlement plan. The committee says its debt settlement plan was accepted by the FEC in May 2026 and its account terminated, yet it still receives notices saying it did not file its quarterly report. Filing.

Gene Douglass for Congress (House candidate committee; Eugene Farley Douglass, R-NC-2 challenger), received 10/16. Says he has not reached the $5,000 threshold and asks that the statement serve as his 12-day pre-general report. Filing.

Greenberg Traurig, P.A. PAC (corporate PAC, type Q), received 10/16. Explains that $13,120.72 in employee payroll deductions from June 15, 2026 was not entered into its reporting system before the July 20, 2026 report was filed, because of an administrative oversight. It says an internal reconciliation found the omission and the PAC amended the July report. Filing.

Heberling for Ohio (House candidate committee; Martin Mathias Heberling III, D-OH challenger), received 10/14. Says the committee has not met the $5,000 threshold for the October Quarterly Report. Filing.

Huerta Democracy PAC (PAC, type O), received 10/16. A letter to FEC analyst Aaron Carrell on its July Quarterly Report (05/14/2026–06/30/2026). Outside counsel is reviewing how the PAC calculated independent expenditures, and the preliminary review indicates some amounts may have been reported on an overinclusive basis. The categories under review are general organizational expenses and compensation, benefits and reimbursements for personnel who did both qualifying federal work and other work. The PAC says it is applying the principle that general overhead not attributable to a specific express-advocacy communication should be excluded. It will file amended reports when the review of hundreds of transactions finishes, and asks for the extra time it discussed with the Reports Analysis Division. Filing.

International Union of Operating Engineers/Local 17 Political Action Committee (union PAC, type Q), received 10/16. Says member contributions need not be itemized because no individual's total reaches the $200 itemization level. Filing.

Jim Priest for US Senate (Senate candidate committee; Jim Priest, D-OK challenger), received 10/15, labeled a loan forgiveness filing. The two-page PDF has no readable text beyond the header, so its contents could not be described. Filing.

Juliana for Illinois (Senate candidate committee; Juliana Stratton, D-IL open seat), received 10/15. Replies to an October 6 FEC letter on its Amended April Quarterly Report (02/26/2026–03/31/2026). Contributions from Andrew McCollum, Kara Baysinger, Jennifer Byrd and Jennifer DiBrienza had incorrect receipt dates; the committee says they arrived outside the 48-hour notice period, so no notices were required, and the dates are corrected. Debts to vendors of $39,871.24 on Line 10 reflect a correction of estimated amounts once final invoices arrived, disclosed in an amended report received 07/15/2026. Signed by treasurer Lauren Decot Lee. Filing.

Karla Kemp Campaign Crew aka Karla Kemp Campaign Fund (House candidate committee; Karla Kemp, D-FL challenger), received 10/15. She says she pulled out of the Florida congressional race and is now the Democratic candidate for a Florida state Senate seat. She says her existing funds were transferred, with donor permission, to the state candidate fund. She says she needs to amend filings because ActBlue activity is missing, and asks whether she should file a termination first, saying she was advised to submit this explanation to buy time. Filing.
Kenfornys24 (House candidate committee; Kenneth Estes, independent NY challenger), received 10/16. Says the campaign had not collected the $5,000 minimum as of 10/15/26. Filing.

Laura Rodriguez-Carbone for Congress (House candidate committee; Laura Rodriguez-Carbone, D-OH challenger), received 10/15, labeled a disavowal response. She disavows any unauthorized campaign or fundraising activity by the committee on her behalf. She states she has not raised or spent, or authorized anyone to raise or spend, more than $5,000, and does not intend to file a statement of candidacy now. Filing.

Luke Nathan Phillips for Congress (House candidate committee; Luke Nathan Phillips, R-VA challenger), received 10/16. Says it had no receipts or disbursements in the period and will submit dissolution paperwork by the end of November. Filing.

Pastor Herrera Macuran for Congress (House candidate committee, FL address), received 10/16. Responding to a notice about the October Quarterly Report due October 15, the candidate says the voluntarily registered committee has never received contributions or made expenditures. The candidate previously submitted a Form 99 about suspending the campaign, and asks the FEC to confirm the report is not required. Filing.
Rampke for President (presidential candidate committee; Daniel Lewis Rampke, Constitution Party), received 10/16. The entire text reads "Nothing." Filing.

Reilly for Montana (Senate candidate committee; Reilly Neill, D-MT open seat), received 10/15. A notice that the candidate forgives her personal loans to the committee, stating the aggregate outstanding principal as $88,100 as of October 14, 2026. It notes this appears in a termination report filed 10/15/26. The attached schedule lists eight loans totaling $88,100 in original amounts, but its "amount forgiven" column shows only $3,000 of the first $7,000 loan forgiven, so the forgiven column totals $84,100, not $88,100. Filing.

Republican Party of Arkansas (state party committee, type Y), received 10/14. Replies to the FEC's September 9, 2026 letter about the description of a disbursement on its July Monthly Report (06/01/2026–06/30/2026). It says it clarified the disbursement in an amended report filed at the same time. Addressed to analyst Aaron Kelley. Filing.

Robert Thomas Gonzalez for Congress (House candidate committee; Robert Thomas Gonzalez, D-CA challenger), received 10/16, first of two. For the October Quarterly it reports $0 raised and $0 spent and says the campaign is "currently not actively active." Filing.

Robert Thomas Gonzalez for Congress, second Form 99 filed two minutes after the first, received 10/16. Also reports $0 raised and spent for the October Quarterly, but says the campaign "is active but will be more active in the Calendar year of 2027," which differs from the first filing's wording. Filing.
Roderick Vereen for Congress (House candidate committee; Roderick D. Vereen, D-FL open seat), received 10/16. Says he did not spend more than $5,000 this quarter. Filing.

Rolling Sea Action Fund (PAC, type V), received 10/16. A supplemental response to an RFAI dated 2/24/2026 on its 2025 Year-End Report. On 10/15/2026 the committee submitted amendments dating back to the first quarter of 2024. It says a self-audit, prompted by the RFAI's cash-on-hand and Line 8 discrepancies, found missing transactions that resolved those discrepancies. Signed by treasurer Jason Hinton, addressed to Aaron Carrell, in care of Kalik and Associates Inc. Filing.

SD PAC (PAC, type W), received 10/16. Replies to an RFAI on its July Monthly Report (06/01/2026–06/30/2026), saying the contribution noted was made to reduce a candidate committee's debts incurred during the primary election. Filing.

Texas Democratic Party (state party committee, type Y), received 10/14. Replies to an RFAI dated September 9, 2026 on its May Monthly Report (4/1/2026–4/30/2026). It says the noted excessive contribution was refunded to the contributor on 9/20/2026 in the amount of $5,000. Signed by treasurer Kendall Scudder, addressed to analyst Melissa Cisewski. Filing.

United Association of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe Fitting Industry (union committee, listed by the FEC as "United Association of J/M & Appr. of PLBG & P/F Industry", type I), notice dated 10/14. This is an FEC Notice of Paper Filing, not a committee-authored statement. It says the committee filed its 48-hour notification report (10/07/2026–10/07/2026, received 10/07/2026) on paper instead of electronically. It cites 11 CFR 104.18, which requires electronic filing above $50,000, and warns that a paper filer may be treated as a nonfiler and face enforcement action. Signed by Compliance Branch Chief Kristin D. Roser. Filing.

Victor4Nevada (House candidate committee; Victor Willert, Nevada, Nonpartisan, challenger), received 10/16. He says the committee received $0 and incurred expenses under $500, and that he is no longer running for Nevada's 1st Congressional District. Filing.

Virginia Ninth Congressional District Democratic Committee (party committee, type X), received 10/15. The one-page Form 99 contains no readable message beyond the committee name and address, so its purpose could not be determined from the PDF. Filing.
Whitney for Texas (House candidate committee; Whitney Masterson-Moyes, D-TX challenger), received 10/16. The entire text is "N/A." Filing.

Yearn Co. Jennifer Tawanda Brown Gaines (Senate candidate committee; Jennifer Tawanda Brown Gaines, Libertarian, TX challenger), received 10/16. A 15-page submission headed "Quarterly reports" with a table of contents (FMR, CDR, FCRA, ROI, NDA, W2, GBP, DNA, 1099) and mostly blank pages. Its few readable lines are unintelligible, and it contains no financial figures. Filing.

sections.headline: Two large negative transactions, both at victory funds
paragraphs: Two new rows of $10,000 or more in negative amounts surfaced. A large negative amount is FEC's convention for a voided, reversed or refunded transaction, usually mundane.

items: Cooper Victory Fund: a $20,000 contribution from John B. Kelly was reversed, dated 2026-07-03, described as a reattribution to Jennifer Epperson from 5/29/26. Transaction.
Whatley Victory Committee: a $25,000 earmarked contribution from David Moritz was reversed, dated 2026-08-31. Transaction.

blocks.text: Itemized receipts of $1,000,000 or more that FEC processed since 10/10/2026 and DC Record hasn't reported before, from FEC Schedule A (2025-26 cycle). Super PACs file monthly or quarterly, so a gift can surface weeks after it was made. Gifts from other committees and organizations are included and labeled.
